title: AMD FY2022 Form 10-K — Item 7 MD&A, segment narratives (Data Center, Client, Gaming, Embedded) and segment reporting change
url: kb_demo/financebench/pdfs/AMD_2022_10K.pdf · p48–p49 (Item 7, MD&A, Results of Operations by segment)
key_points: During Q2 fiscal 2022 AMD changed its reporting segments to align financial reporting with how it manages the business in strategic end markets.

Data Center net revenue of $6 billion in 2022 increased 64%, primarily driven by higher EPYC server processor sales; Data Center operating income rose to $1.8 billion from $991 million on higher revenue, partly offset by higher operating expenses.

Client net revenue of $6.2 billion in 2022 decreased 10%, driven by a 24% decrease in unit shipments, partly offset by a 19% increase in average selling price, due to challenging PC market conditions.
Gaming net revenue of $6.8 billion in 2022 increased 21%, driven by higher semi-custom console SoC sales, partly offset by lower gaming graphics sales.

Embedded net revenue of $4.6 billion in 2022 increased significantly versus $246 million in 2021, primarily driven by the inclusion of Xilinx embedded product revenue following the February 2022 acquisition.
Embedded operating income was $2.3 billion in 2022 versus $44 million in 2021, with the significant increase attributed to the Xilinx acquisition.

Client net revenue of $6.2 billion in 2022 decreased by 10%, compared to net revenue of $6.9 billion in 2021, primarily driven by a 24% decrease in unit shipment, partially offset by a 19% increase in average selling price. ...
